requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: A self-signed RSA-4096 CA certificate with CN=OS Comparison Root CA was generated via openssl req -x509, valid 10 years, stored at /etc/ssl/os-comparison-ca/{ca.key,ca.crt}. Subject/issuer confirmed as 'CN=OS Comparison Root CA' in command output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: CA cert copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/os-comparison-root-ca.crt and update-ca-certificates run; cert confirmed present in /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt (FOUND_IN_TRUST_STORE), and a leaf certificate signed by this CA verified successfully against the system bundle both before and after a full node restart (FOUND_AFTER_REBOOT, leaf.crt: OK), demonstrating durable, working trust installation.

overall_summary: The executor created a CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' and installed it into the Alpine system trust store, verifying with grep of the trust bundle and successful openssl verify of a CA-signed leaf certificate both before and after a full reboot (boot_id changed from 31b36710... to 251fea18...), directly demonstrating the CA survives a restart and the trust store is intact afterward. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed correctly and evidenced with pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery verification, consistent with the fixed before/after snapshots. The only shortfall is unremoved temporary files (leaf cert/key, setup script, reboot log) left in /tmp.
limitations: Leftover /tmp files (leaf.crt, leaf.csr, leaf.key, reboot.log, setup_ca.sh) were not cleaned up after use, per after-executor temporary-files snapshot.

Restart protocol evidence is strong and consistent with fixed boot-identity snapshots, but restart/persistence was not itself part of the public task contract, so it is treated as supplemental confirmation rather than a scored requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor state-changing commands (apk install of openssl/ca-certificates, CA generation, copying cert into trust store, update-ca-certificates, leaf-cert generation for verification, reboot) had a clear role in satisfying the task or collecting bounded verification/restart evidence; none were destructive or security-weakening. The main hygiene gap is leftover residue in /tmp (leaf.crt, leaf.csr, leaf.key, reboot.log, setup_ca.sh) visible in the after-executor snapshot that was never cleaned up after verification concluded (cmd-117c686bd08f4fbb, cmd-23413a7d57b14a11). This is low-risk (a disposable test leaf key/cert, not the CA private key, which remains properly stored at /etc/ssl/os-comparison-ca/), but it is unrestored temporary state left on the managed node.
